title.zh: 卷一百二十三 載記第二十三 慕容垂
title.raw: 卷一百二十三 載記第二十三 慕容垂 Volume 123 Records 23: Murong Chui

sentences.zh: 慕容垂

translations.literal: Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂，字道明，皝之第五子也。

translations.literal: Murong Chui, courtesy name Daoming, was the fifth son of Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui, styled Daoming, was Murong Huang's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 少岐嶷有器度，身長七尺七寸，手垂過膝。

translations.literal: In youth he was precocious and possessed breadth of character; he stood seven feet seven inches tall, and his hands hung past his knees.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was sharp and commanding; he grew to seven feet seven inches, with hands that reached below his knees.

sentences.zh: 皝甚寵之，常目而謂諸弟曰：「此兒闊達好奇，終能破人家，或能成人家。

translations.literal: Huang greatly favored him and would often fix his gaze on him and say to his other sons: "This boy is broad-minded and curious by nature; in the end he will be able to ruin a household—or perhaps to establish one.
translations.idiomatic: Huang doted on him. He would often stare at the boy and tell his other sons, "This one is open-handed and restless; in time he may wreck a house—or build one.

sentences.zh: 」故名霸，字道業，恩遇逾於世子俊，故俊不能平之。

translations.literal: Therefore he was named Ba, courtesy name Daoye; the favor shown him exceeded that shown to the heir Jun, so Jun could not be reconciled to it.
translations.idiomatic: So he was named Ba, with the style Daoye, and was favored even above the heir Jun—something Jun never forgave.

sentences.zh: 以滅宇文之功，封都鄉侯。

translations.literal: For his achievement in destroying the Yuwen, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of the Capital District.
translations.idiomatic: For the campaign that destroyed the Yuwen, he was made marquis of the capital district.

sentences.zh: 石季龍來伐，既還，猶有兼併之志，遣將鄧恆率眾數萬屯于樂安，營攻取之備。

translations.literal: When Shi Hu came to attack and then withdrew, he still harbored designs of annexation, sending the general Deng Heng with tens of thousands of troops to camp at Le'an and making preparations to attack and seize it.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Hu invaded and withdrew, Huang still meant to swallow more territory. He sent Deng Heng with tens of thousands of men to camp at Le'an and prepare an assault.

sentences.zh: 垂戍徒河，與恆相持，恆憚而不敢侵。

translations.literal: Chui garrisoned Tuhe and confronted Heng; Heng feared him and did not dare invade.
translations.idiomatic: Chui held Tuhe and faced Heng across the lines; Heng was afraid to press the attack.

sentences.zh: 垂少好畋遊，因獵墜馬折齒，慕容俊僭即王位，改名𡙇，外以慕郤𡙇為名，內實惡而改之。

translations.literal: In youth Chui loved hunting; while hunting he fell from his horse and broke his teeth. When Murong Jun presumptuously took the royal title, he changed Chui's name to Guai—outwardly in homage to Xi Que, inwardly because he hated that name and changed it.
translations.idiomatic: Chui loved the chase in his youth and once broke his teeth in a fall from his horse. When Murong Jun declared himself king, he renamed Chui Guai—ostensibly after Xi Que, in truth because he loathed the old name.

sentences.zh: 尋以讖記之文，乃去「夬」，以「垂」為名焉。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, on the basis of prophetic texts, he removed the "guai" component and took "Chui" as his name.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a prophecy led him to drop the guai radical and fix the name as Chui.

sentences.zh: 石季龍之死也，趙魏亂，垂謂俊曰：「時來易失，赴機在速，兼弱攻昧，今其時矣。

translations.literal: When Shi Hu died, Zhao and Wei fell into disorder. Chui said to Jun: "Opportune moments are easily lost; seizing chance depends on speed. Attacking the weak while they are benighted—now is the time.
translations.idiomatic: At Shi Hu's death the north collapsed into chaos. Chui told Jun, "Moments slip away; speed is everything. Strike the weak while they are blind—that hour is now.

sentences.zh: 」俊以新遭大喪，不許。

translations.literal: Jun, having newly suffered a major bereavement, did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Jun, still deep in mourning, refused.

sentences.zh: 慕輿根言於俊曰：「王子之言，千載一時，不可失也。

translations.literal: Murong Gen said to Jun: "The prince's words mark a moment that comes once in a thousand years—it must not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Gen urged Jun, "What the prince says is a once-in-a-thousand-years chance. Let it not pass.

sentences.zh: 」俊乃從之，以垂為前鋒都督。

translations.literal: Jun then followed his advice and made Chui commander of the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Jun relented and named Chui commander of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 俊既克幽州，將坑降卒，垂諫曰：「吊伐之義，先代常典。

translations.literal: After Jun had taken Youzhou, he was about to bury alive the surrendered soldiers. Chui remonstrated: "The principle of succoring the fallen while punishing the guilty was a constant practice of former ages.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun seized Youzhou he meant to massacre the captives. Chui protested, "Succoring the fallen and punishing the guilty was the old way of kings.

sentences.zh: 今方平中原，宜綏懷以德，坑戮之刑不可為王師之先聲。

translations.literal: Now as we are about to pacify the Central Plains, we ought to soothe and embrace them with virtue; the punishment of mass slaughter must not be the first note struck by the royal army.
translations.idiomatic: As we move to pacify the heartland, win men with kindness. Mass killing must not be the first sound our armies make.

sentences.zh: 」俊從之。

translations.literal: Jun accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: Jun agreed.

sentences.zh: 及俊僭稱尊號，封垂吳王，徙鎮信都，以侍中、右禁將軍錄留台事，大收東北之利。

translations.literal: When Jun presumptuously assumed the exalted title, he enfeoffed Chui as Prince of Wu, transferred him to garrison Xindu, made him recorder of affairs at the capital garrison with the titles of palace attendant and right forbidden general, and greatly drew profit from the northeast.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun took the imperial title he made Chui prince of Wu and posted him at Xindu as palace attendant, right forbidden general, and recorder of the eastern capital, drawing heavy revenue from the northeast.

sentences.zh: 又為征南將軍、荊、兗二州牧，有聲于梁、楚之南。

translations.literal: He was also made General Who Campaigns South and governor of Jing and Yan provinces, winning renown south of Liang and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: He was also named general who campaigns south and governor of Jing and Yan, famed throughout the lands south of Liang and Chu.

sentences.zh: 再為司隸，偽王公已下莫不累跡。

translations.literal: He served again as metropolitan commandant, and none of the false kings and dukes and below did not tread in his wake.
translations.idiomatic: A second term as metropolitan commandant followed; every prince and minister in the realm trailed in his wake.

sentences.zh: 時莫容暐嗣偽位，慕容恪為太宰。

translations.literal: At this time Murong Wei succeeded to the false throne, with Murong Ke as grand preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Wei now held the throne and Murong Ke served as grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 恪甚重垂，常謂暐曰：「吳王將相之才十倍於臣，先帝以長幼之次，以臣先之，臣死之後，願陛下委政吳王，可謂親賢兼舉。

translations.literal: Ke greatly valued Chui and often said to Wei: "The Prince of Wu's talent as general and minister is ten times mine. The former emperor, following the order of seniority, placed me before him. After I die, I hope Your Majesty will entrust government to the Prince of Wu—one may call this honoring the worthy while elevating one's kin.
translations.idiomatic: Ke esteemed Chui and often told Wei, "The Prince of Wu has ten times my gifts as statesman and commander. Our late lord, respecting age, set me ahead of him. When I am gone, entrust the realm to the Prince of Wu—that is how to honor talent and kin together.

sentences.zh: 」及敗桓溫於枋頭，威名大振。

translations.literal: When he defeated Huan Wen at Fangtou, his prestige and name greatly expanded.
translations.idiomatic: After he shattered Huan Wen at Fangtou, his fame soared.

sentences.zh: 慕容評深忌惡之，乃謀誅垂。

translations.literal: Murong Ping deeply resented and hated him and plotted to kill Chui.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Ping hated him bitterly and plotted his death.

sentences.zh: 垂懼禍及己，與世子全奔於苻堅。

translations.literal: Chui feared disaster would reach him and fled with the heir Quan to Fu Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing for his life, Chui fled with his heir Murong Quan to Fu Jian.

sentences.zh: 自恪卒後，堅密有圖暐之謀，憚垂威名而未發。

translations.literal: After Ke's death, Jian secretly cherished plans to take Wei but feared Chui's prestige and name and did not act.
translations.idiomatic: After Ke died, Jian quietly planned to destroy Yan but held back for fear of Chui's name.

sentences.zh: 及聞其至，堅大悅，郊迎執手，禮之甚重。

translations.literal: When he heard Chui had arrived, Jian was greatly pleased, went to the suburbs to welcome him, took his hand, and treated him with the utmost honor.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Chui had come, Jian went out to meet him, clasped his hand, and honored him lavishly.

sentences.zh: 堅相王猛惡垂雄略，勸堅殺之。

translations.literal: Jian's chief minister Wang Meng hated Chui's heroic stratagems and urged Jian to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Meng, Jian's chief minister, feared Chui's genius and urged execution.

sentences.zh: 堅不從，以為冠軍將軍，封賓都侯，食華陰之五百戶。

translations.literal: Jian did not follow this advice, instead making him general of the champions and enfeoffing him Marquis of Bin Capital, with a fief of five hundred households in Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: Jian refused. He made Chui general of the champions, marquis of Bin Capital, with five hundred households in Huayin.

sentences.zh: 王猛伐洛，引全為參軍。

translations.literal: When Wang Meng campaigned against Luoyang, he took Quan as aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Meng marched on Luoyang he took Quan on his staff.

sentences.zh: 猛乃令人詭傳垂語于全曰：「吾已東還，汝可為計也。

translations.literal: Meng then had someone falsely spread word to Quan in Chui's name: "I have already returned east—you may make your plans.
translations.idiomatic: Meng forged a message to Quan in Chui's name: "I have gone east. Act as you see fit.

sentences.zh: 」全信之，乃奔暐。

translations.literal: Quan believed it and fled to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Quan believed it and fled back to Murong Wei.

sentences.zh: 猛表全叛狀，垂懼而東奔，及藍田，為追騎所獲。

translations.literal: Meng memorialized Quan's act of rebellion; Chui feared and fled east, and at Lantian was captured by pursuing horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Meng reported Quan's defection. Chui fled east in alarm and was caught at Lantian by pursuers.

sentences.zh: 堅引見東堂，慰勉之曰：「卿家國失和，委身投朕。

translations.literal: Jian received him in the eastern hall and comforted him: "Your house and state lost harmony and you entrusted yourself to me.
translations.idiomatic: Jian received him in the eastern hall and said, "Your house fell out and you came to me.

sentences.zh: 賢子志不忘本，猶懷首丘。

translations.literal: Your worthy son, mindful of his origins, still yearned for his old hills.
translations.idiomatic: Your fine son remembered his roots and longed for home.

sentences.zh: 《書》不云乎：「父父子子，無相及也。

translations.literal: Does not the Book say: "Father is father, son is son—the guilty do not implicate one another"?
translations.idiomatic: Does not the Book say, "Father and son each keep his place—guilt does not cross generations"?

sentences.zh: 」卿何為過懼而狼狽若斯也！

translations.literal: Why do you pass alarm to such a degree of panic!
translations.idiomatic: Why such panic?

sentences.zh: 」於是復垂爵位，恩待如初。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chui's rank and titles were restored and he was treated with favor as before.
translations.idiomatic: Chui's rank was restored and he was favored as before.

sentences.zh: 及堅擒暐，垂隨堅入鄴，收集諸子，對之悲慟，見其故吏，有不悅之色。

translations.literal: When Jian captured Wei, Chui followed Jian into Ye, gathered his sons, and wept bitterly before them; when he saw his former officials, some showed displeasure.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian took Ye, Chui entered with him, gathered his sons, and wept before them; some old officers he greeted with a scowl.

sentences.zh: 前郎中令高弼私於垂曰：「大王以命世之姿，遭無妄之運，迍邅棲伏，艱亦至矣。

translations.literal: The former director of palace attendants Gao Bi said privately to Chui: "Great King, with a stature of one who commands an age, you have met with undeserved fortune, dwelling in hardship and seclusion—the hardship has indeed been extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Bi, former director of palace attendants, said privately, "Great King, born for an age of turmoil, you have suffered misfortune and lived in hiding—the trial has been severe.

sentences.zh: 天啟嘉會，靈命暫遷，此乃鴻漸之始，龍變之初，深願仁慈有以慰之。

translations.literal: Heaven has opened a blessed conjunction; for a moment the mandate rests with you—this is the beginning of the wild goose's ascent, the first change of the dragon. I deeply hope you will show mercy to comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven now offers a turn of fortune; for a moment the mandate is yours—the wild goose begins its flight, the dragon stirs. Show mercy and comfort these men.

sentences.zh: 且夫高世之略必懷遺俗之規，方當網漏吞舟，以弘苞養之義；

translations.literal: Moreover, the strategy of one who towers above his age must cherish rules that leave custom behind; at this juncture one should let the net slack so it may swallow great fish, thereby to enlarge the meaning of sheltering and nurturing;
translations.idiomatic: Great designs require magnanimity. Loosen the net to take big fish—enlarge the grace of sheltering and nurturing;

sentences.zh: 收納舊臣之胄，以成為山之功，奈何以一怒捐之？

translations.literal: gather the offspring of old ministers to complete the merit of forming a mountain—how can you cast them aside in a fit of anger?
translations.idiomatic: gather the sons of your old officers and build a mountain of loyalty. Why cast them off in anger?

sentences.zh: 竊為大王不取。

translations.literal: I venture to think this unworthy of Great King.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Great King not to do this.

sentences.zh: 」垂深納之。

translations.literal: Chui deeply accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: Chui took the advice to heart.

sentences.zh: 垂在堅朝，歷位京兆尹，進封泉州侯，所在征伐，皆在大功。

translations.literal: While Chui served in Jian's court he held the post of metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, was advanced to Marquis of Quanzhou, and in campaigns wherever he went, the greatest achievements were his.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jian he governed Jingzhao, rose to marquis of Quanzhou, and in every campaign carried off the chief honors.

sentences.zh: 堅之敗於淮南也，垂軍獨全，堅以千餘騎奔垂。

translations.literal: When Jian was defeated at Huainan, Chui's army alone remained intact; Jian fled to Chui with a thousand-odd horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: At the defeat on the Huai, only Chui's corps held together. Jian fled to him with a thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 垂世子寶言於垂曰：「家國傾喪，皇綱廢馳，至尊明命著之圖籙，當隆中興之業，建少康之功。

translations.literal: Chui's heir Bao said to Chui: "House and state have collapsed, the imperial norm lies in ruins—the Supreme One's bright mandate is recorded in the charts; you should raise the enterprise of restoration and build the achievement of Shaokang.
translations.idiomatic: Bao urged Chui, "Our house is ruined and the throne empty, yet heaven's mandate is written in the charts. Raise the restoration as Shaokang did.

sentences.zh: 但時來之運未至，故韜光俟奮耳。

translations.literal: But the fortune of the hour had not yet come, so he hid his light and waited to soar.
translations.idiomatic: The hour had not come, so you hid your light and waited.

sentences.zh: 今天厭亂德，凶眾土崩，可謂乾啟神機，授之於我。

translations.literal: Now Heaven loathes disorderly virtue, the evil masses crumble like earth—one may say the Qian trigram has opened the divine opportunity and handed it to us.
translations.idiomatic: Now heaven hates Qin's crimes and its hosts crumble. The divine moment is ours.

sentences.zh: 千載一時，今其會也，宜恭承皇天之意，因而取之。

translations.literal: A moment that comes once in a millennium—now is the conjunction. You ought respectfully to receive Heaven's intent and take it accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: A once-in-a-thousand-years chance is here. Receive heaven's will and seize it.

sentences.zh: 且夫立大功者不顧小節，行大仁者不念小惠。

translations.literal: Moreover, one who establishes great achievement does not fuss over minor points; one who practices great humanity does not dwell on small favors.
translations.idiomatic: Great deeds ignore small scruples; great kindness forgets petty debts.

sentences.zh: 秦既蕩覆二京，空辱神器，仇恥之深，莫甚於此，願不以意氣微恩而忘社稷之重。

translations.literal: Qin has already overthrown the two capitals and shamed the sacred regalia—the depth of enmity and shame could hardly be greater. I hope you will not, for a trifling personal favor, forget the weight of altars and state.
translations.idiomatic: Qin wrecked the two capitals and defiled the throne—the shame is beyond measure. Do not let one man's kindness outweigh the altars of Yan.

sentences.zh: 五木之祥，今其至矣。

translations.literal: The omen of the five tablets—now it has come.
translations.idiomatic: The omen of the five tablets has come true.

sentences.zh: 」垂曰：「汝言是也。

translations.literal: Chui said: "Your words are right.
translations.idiomatic: Chui said, "You are right.

sentences.zh: 然彼以赤心投命，若何害之！

translations.literal: Yet he came placing his red heart in our hands—how could I harm him!
translations.idiomatic: Yet he came to us in good faith—how can I strike him down!

sentences.zh: 苟天所棄，圖之多便。

translations.literal: If Heaven has abandoned him, there will be ample opportunity to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: If heaven has cast him off, we will have many chances to act.

sentences.zh: 且縱令北還，更待其釁，既不負宿心，可以義取天下。

translations.literal: And even if we let him return north, we may wait for further provocation; having not betrayed my longstanding intent, one may yet take the realm by righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: Let him go north and wait for his next mistake. Keep faith with him for now, and take the realm by righteous means later."

sentences.zh: 」垂弟德進曰：「夫鄰國相吞，有自來矣。

translations.literal: Chui's younger brother De advanced and said: "The swallowing of neighboring states has existed from of old.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Murong De pressed him: "States have always swallowed their neighbors.

sentences.zh: 秦強而並燕，秦弱而圖之，此為報仇雪辱，豈所謂負宿心也！

translations.literal: When Qin was strong it annexed Yan; when Qin is weak we plot against it. This is to repay enmity and wipe away shame—how can it be called betraying one's longstanding intent!
translations.idiomatic: Qin swallowed Yan when it was strong; now that Qin is weak we strike back. That is vengeance, not betrayal!

sentences.zh: 昔鄧祁侯不納三甥之言，終為楚所滅；

translations.literal: In former times the Marquis of Deng did not heed the words of his three nephews and was destroyed by Chu in the end;
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Deng ignored his nephews' warning and was destroyed by Chu;

sentences.zh: 吳王夫差違子胥之諫，取禍句踐。

translations.literal: King Fuchai of Wu defied Zixu's remonstrance and brought disaster from Goujian.
translations.idiomatic: King Fuchai of Wu spurned Wu Zixu and fell to Goujian.

sentences.zh: 前事之不忘，後事之師表也。

translations.literal: Not to forget what went before is the teacher of what comes after.
translations.idiomatic: The past is the mirror of the future.

sentences.zh: 願不棄湯、武之成蹤，追韓信之敗跡，乘彼土崩，恭行天罰，斬逆氐，復宗祀，建中興，繼洪烈，天下大機，弗宜失也。

translations.literal: I hope you will not abandon the completed footprints of Tang and Wu, but follow the failed track of Han Xin—while their earth crumbles, respectfully execute Heaven's punishment, cut down the rebellious Di, restore the ancestral sacrifices, establish restoration, and continue the great enterprise. The great opportunity of the realm must not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Do not spurn the example of Tang and Wu for Han Xin's folly. While Qin collapses, execute heaven's judgment, destroy the Di, restore our altars, and rebuild the dynasty. Do not lose the realm's great chance.

sentences.zh: 若釋數萬之眾，授幹將之柄，是郤天時而待後害，非至計也。

translations.literal: If you release tens of thousands of troops and hand over the hilt of the Ganjiang, you reject Heaven's season and wait for harm to come later—not the supreme plan.
translations.idiomatic: Release tens of thousands of men and hand Jian the sword—that rejects heaven's season and invites later ruin. It is no master plan.

sentences.zh: 語曰：'當斷不斷，反受其亂。

translations.literal: The saying goes: "He who will not decide when he should must will suffer disorder."
translations.idiomatic: As the proverb says, "He who will not decide when he must will be undone by disorder."

sentences.zh: '願兄無疑。

translations.literal: I hope Elder Brother will have no doubts."
translations.idiomatic: Brother, have no doubts."

sentences.zh: 」垂曰：「吾昔為太傅所不容，投身于秦主，又為王猛所譖，復見昭亮，國士之禮每深，報德之分未一。

translations.literal: Chui said: "In former days the grand preceptor would not tolerate me; I cast myself on the Lord of Qin and was again slandered by Wang Meng, yet again shown clear discernment—the courtesy due a national warrior was always deep, but the portion of repaying kindness remains unfulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Chui said, "Ke once drove me out; Jian took me in. Wang Meng slandered me, yet Jian cleared me. He treated me as a peer of the realm, and I have not repaid him.

sentences.zh: 如使秦運必窮，歷數歸我者，授首之便，何慮無之。

translations.literal: If Qin's fortune must indeed reach its end and the cycles return to us, the convenience of taking his head—why worry that it will not come!
translations.idiomatic: If Qin's fate is spent and the mandate returns to us, his head will be easy to take.

sentences.zh: 關西之地，會非吾有，自當有擾之者，吾可端拱而定關東。

translations.literal: The lands west of the Pass were never mine to have; there will naturally be those who disturb them—I may sit with folded hands and pacify the east of the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: The west was never ours; others will fight over it. I can sit at ease and secure the east.

sentences.zh: 君子不怙亂，不為禍先，且可觀之。

translations.literal: A gentleman does not rely on disorder and does not beget calamity first—let us observe for now."
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman does not profit from chaos or strike first. Let us watch."

sentences.zh: 」乃以兵屬堅。

translations.literal: Thereupon he handed his troops over to Jian.
translations.idiomatic: He gave his troops back to Jian.

sentences.zh: 初，寶在長安，與韓黃、李根等因讌摴蒱，寶危坐整容，誓之曰：「世云摴蒱有神，豈虛也哉！

translations.literal: Earlier, when Bao was in Chang'an, with Han Huang, Li Gen, and others he played divination tiles at a banquet; Bao sat upright with composed countenance and vowed: "The world says divination tiles have a spirit—is it empty talk!
translations.idiomatic: Earlier in Chang'an, Bao played tile dice with Han Huang and Li Gen. Sitting straight, he vowed, "They say the dice have a spirit—is it true?

sentences.zh: 若富貴可期，頻得三盧。

translations.literal: If wealth and honor may be expected, may I throw three "lu" in succession."
translations.idiomatic: If fortune is near, let me throw three lu in a row."

sentences.zh: 」於是三擲盡盧，寶拜而受賜，故云五木之祥。

translations.literal: Thereupon on three throws he got lu throughout; Bao bowed to receive the blessing—hence the saying of the omen of the five tablets.
translations.idiomatic: He threw three times and got lu each time. Bao bowed in thanks—hence the omen of the five tablets.

sentences.zh: 堅至澠池，垂請至鄴展拜陵墓，因張國威刑，以安戎狄。

translations.literal: When Jian reached Mianchi, Chui requested to go to Ye to pay respects at the tombs, and thereby display the state's authority and punishments to settle the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: At Mianchi Chui asked leave to visit the tombs at Ye and show Qin's majesty to the frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 堅許之，權翼諫曰：「垂爪牙名將，所謂今之韓、白，世豪東夏，志不為人用。

translations.literal: Jian consented; Quan Yi remonstrated: "Chui is a famed general among claws and fangs—the so-called Han Xin and Bai Qi of today, a magnate of the eastern Xia whose will is not to serve others.
translations.idiomatic: Jian agreed. Quan Yi warned, "Chui is a tiger among generals—the Han Xin or Bai Qi of our day, a lord of the eastern lands who serves no master willingly.

sentences.zh: 頃以避禍歸誠，非慕德而至，列土幹城未可以滿其志，冠軍之號豈足以稱其心！

translations.literal: He recently came placing himself under us to escape disaster—not from admiration of virtue. Territory and the shield of the realm cannot satisfy his ambition; the title general of the champions can hardly content his heart!
translations.idiomatic: He came only to escape ruin, not from love of our virtue. Lands and titles cannot fill his ambition; the rank of champion general cannot satisfy him.

sentences.zh: 且垂猶鷹也，饑則附人，飽便高颺，遇風塵之會，必有陵霄之志。

translations.literal: Moreover Chui is like a hawk: when hungry he clings to men, when full he soars high—meet wind and dust and he will surely have the will to tower above the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: He is like a hawk: hungry, he perches on your wrist; fed, he flies away. Give him turmoil and he will rise above the clouds.

sentences.zh: 惟宜急其羈靽，不可任其所欲。

translations.literal: You should only hurry to bind his reins—do not let him have his desire."
translations.idiomatic: Bind him quickly. Do not let him have his way."

sentences.zh: 」堅不從，遣其將李蠻、閔亮、尹國率眾三千送垂，又遣石越戍鄴，張蠔戍并州。

translations.literal: Jian did not follow this, sending his generals Li Man, Min Liang, and Yin Guo with three thousand troops to escort Chui, and also sent Shi Yue to garrison Ye and Zhang Mang to garrison Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jian refused. He sent Li Man, Min Liang, and Yin Guo with three thousand men to escort Chui, posted Shi Yue at Ye and Zhang Mang at Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時堅子丕先在鄴，及垂至，丕館之於鄴西，垂具說淮南敗狀。

translations.literal: At this time Jian's son Pi was already at Ye; when Chui arrived, Pi lodged him west of Ye, and Chui gave a full account of the defeat at Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's son Fu Pi was already at Ye. Pi lodged Chui west of the city and heard his account of the Huai defeat.

sentences.zh: 會堅將苻暉告丁零翟斌聚眾謀逼洛陽，歪謂垂曰：「惟斌兄弟因王師小失，敢肆凶勃，子母之軍，殆難為敵，非冠軍英略，莫可以滅也。

translations.literal: It happened that Jian's general Fu Hui reported that the Dingling Zhai Bin had gathered troops plotting to press Luoyang. Pi said to Chui: "Only the Bin brothers, relying on our army's small setback, dare unleash violence—the mother-and-son army will be hard to match; none but the champion's heroic design can destroy them. Might I trouble you with one campaign?
translations.idiomatic: Fu Hui reported that Zhai Bin of the Dingling had raised troops against Luoyang. Pi told Chui, "The Bins exploit our setback. Their host will be hard to break—only your genius can crush them. Will you go?

sentences.zh: 欲相煩一行可乎？

translations.literal: Might I trouble you to go on one campaign?
translations.idiomatic: Will you take the field?

sentences.zh: 」垂曰：「下官殿下之鷹犬，敢不惟命是聽。

translations.literal: Chui said: "Your low servant is Your Highness's hawk and hound—how dare I not obey as commanded!
translations.idiomatic: Chui said, "I am Your Highness's hound. Command me.

sentences.zh: 」於是大賜金帛，一無所受，惟請舊田園。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was lavishly gifted gold and silk but accepted none, requesting only his former fields and gardens.
translations.idiomatic: Pi offered gold and silk in profusion; Chui took none, asking only for his old estates.

sentences.zh: 丕許之，配垂兵二千，遣其將苻飛龍率氐騎一千為垂之副。

translations.literal: Pi consented, assigned Chui two thousand troops, and sent his general Fu Feilong with a thousand Di cavalry as Chui's deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Pi agreed, gave him two thousand men, and sent Fu Feilong with a thousand Di horse as his lieutenant.

sentences.zh: 丕戒飛龍曰：「卿王室肺腑，年秩雖卑，其實帥也。

translations.literal: Pi warned Feilong: "You are flesh and blood of the royal house; though young in years, in truth you are the commander.
translations.idiomatic: Pi told Feilong, "You are of the royal blood. Young as you are, you are the true commander.

sentences.zh: 垂為三軍之統，卿為謀垂之主，用兵制勝之權，防微杜貳之略，委之於卿，卿其勉之。

translations.literal: Chui is commander of the three armies—you are master of plotting against Chui; the authority to employ troops and achieve victory, the strategy of guarding against the slightest sign of rebellion—all is entrusted to you. Do your utmost."
translations.idiomatic: Chui leads the army—you watch Chui. All power to command, all plans to check rebellion are yours. Be vigilant."

sentences.zh: 」垂請入鄴城拜廟，丕不許。

translations.literal: Chui requested to enter Ye city to pay respects at the temple; Pi did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Chui asked to enter Ye and bow at the ancestral shrine. Pi refused.

sentences.zh: 乃潛服而入，亭吏禁之，垂怒，斬吏燒亭而去。

translations.literal: He then entered in secret dress; the pavilion clerk barred him. Chui grew angry, beheaded the clerk, burned the pavilion, and left.
translations.idiomatic: He slipped in disguised. A clerk stopped him. Chui killed the clerk, burned the post, and left.

sentences.zh: 石越言於丕曰：「垂之在燕，破國亂家，及投命聖朝，蒙超常之遇，忽敢輕侮方鎮，殺吏焚亭，反形已露，終為亂階。

translations.literal: Shi Yue said to Pi: "When Chui was in Yan he ruined states and overturned households; coming to entrust himself to the holy dynasty he received favor surpassing the normal—yet he dares lightly insult a frontier commander, kill an official, and burn a pavilion; his rebellious aspect is already exposed and in the end he will be a source of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yue told Pi, "Chui wrecked Yan and fled here. You favored him beyond measure, yet he kills your men and burns your posts. His rebellion is plain.

sentences.zh: 將老兵疲，可襲而取之矣。

translations.literal: The troops are weary and veterans spent—you may strike and take him."
translations.idiomatic: His men are tired. Strike now and take him."

sentences.zh: 」歪曰：「淮南之敗，眾散親離，而垂侍衛聖躬，誠不可忘。

translations.literal: Pi said: "At the defeat at Huainan the masses scattered and kin were lost, yet Chui attended and guarded the sacred person—indeed this cannot be forgotten."
translations.idiomatic: Pi said, "At the Huai he stood by my father when all else fled. That debt stands."

sentences.zh: 」越曰：「垂既不忠於燕，其肯盡忠於我乎！

translations.literal: Yue said: "Chui was already disloyal to Yan—will he be wholly loyal to us!
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "He betrayed Yan. Why trust him with Qin?

sentences.zh: 且其亡虜也，主上寵同功舊，不能銘澤誓忠，而首謀為亂，今不擊之，必為後害。

translations.literal: Moreover he is a fugitive whom the sovereign honored like a meritorious elder; he could not inscribe kindness in his heart and swear loyalty, but instead took the lead in plotting rebellion—if we do not strike now, he will surely harm us later."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor treated this fugitive like an old comrade, and he repays us with revolt. If we do not strike, he will destroy us."

sentences.zh: 」丕不從。

translations.literal: Pi did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Pi would not listen.

sentences.zh: 越退而告人曰：「公父子好存小仁，不顧天下大計，吾屬終當為鮮卑虜矣。」

translations.literal: Yue withdrew and told others: "The lord father and son love to preserve small humanity and disregard the great plan for the realm—we in the end will become captives of the Xianbei."
translations.idiomatic: Yue left muttering, "Father and son cherish petty kindness and forget the realm. We will end as Xianbei captives."

sentences.zh: 垂至河內，殺飛龍，悉誅氐兵，召募遠近，眾至三萬，濟河焚橋，令曰：「吾本外假秦聲，內規興復。

translations.literal: When Chui reached Henei he killed Feilong, executed all the Di troops, summoned recruits from near and far until his force reached thirty thousand; crossing the river he burned the bridge and issued an order: "I have outwardly borrowed Qin's name while inwardly planning restoration.
translations.idiomatic: At Henei Chui killed Feilong and slaughtered the Di escort. Recruits swelled his ranks to thirty thousand. He crossed the river, burned the bridge, and proclaimed, "Outwardly I served Qin; inwardly I meant to restore Yan.

sentences.zh: 亂法者軍有常刑，奉命者賞不逾日，天下既定，封爵有差，不相負也。」

translations.literal: Those who disturb discipline will face the army's standing punishment; those who obey commands will be rewarded within the day. When the realm is settled, titles and fiefs will be apportioned by rank—none will be shortchanged."
translations.idiomatic: Break discipline and face military law; obey and be rewarded within the day. When the realm is won, ranks and fiefs will be justly given. I will not cheat you."

sentences.zh: 翟斌聞垂之將濟河也，遣使推垂為盟主。

translations.literal: When Zhai Bin heard that Chui was about to cross the river, he sent envoys to urge Chui to become league chief.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Chui meant to cross the river, Zhai Bin sent envoys offering him leadership of the league.

sentences.zh: 垂距之曰：「吾父子寄命秦朝，危而獲濟，荷主上不世之恩，蒙更生之惠，雖曰君臣，義深父子，豈可因其小隙，便懷二三。

translations.literal: Chui refused, saying: "My father and I entrusted our lives to the Qin court; in peril we were saved and received our sovereign's unexampled grace and the favor of renewed life. Though called minister and lord, our bond is as deep as father and son—how could I, for a small grievance, harbor divided loyalties?
translations.idiomatic: Chui declined: "My father and I found refuge in Qin. In danger we were spared; the emperor gave us life anew. Though we are called subject and lord, our bond is like father and son. How could I turn on him for a slight?

sentences.zh: 吾本救豫州，不赴君等，何為斯議而及於我！

translations.literal: My purpose was to rescue Yuzhou and not to join you—why does this proposal reach me!
translations.idiomatic: I came to save Yuzhou, not to join your revolt. Why drag me into this?

sentences.zh: 」垂進欲襲據洛陽，故見苻暉以臣節，退又未審斌之誠款，故以此言距之。

translations.literal: Chui wished to advance and seize Luoyang by surprise, so he showed Fu Hui the deference due a subject; then, not yet sure of Bin's sincerity, he used these words to refuse him.
translations.idiomatic: Chui meant to take Luoyang by surprise, so he played the loyal subject before Fu Hui; uncertain of Bin's loyalty, he answered with this refusal.

sentences.zh: 垂至洛陽，暉閉門距守，不與垂通。

translations.literal: When Chui reached Luoyang, Hui shut the gates and held defense, refusing contact with Chui.
translations.idiomatic: At Luoyang, Hui barred the gates and would not receive Chui.

sentences.zh: 斌又遣長史河南郭通說垂，乃許之。

translations.literal: Bin again sent his chief clerk Guo Tong of Henan to persuade Chui, and Chui then consented.
translations.idiomatic: Bin sent his clerk Guo Tong to win Chui over, and Chui agreed.

sentences.zh: 斌率眾會垂，勸稱尊號，垂曰：「新興侯，國之正統，孤之君也。

translations.literal: Bin led his troops to join Chui and urged him to assume the exalted title. Chui said: "The Marquis of Xinxing is the legitimate ruler of the state—he is my lord.
translations.idiomatic: Bin joined Chui and urged him to take the throne. Chui said, "Fu Pi is the rightful heir. He is my sovereign.

sentences.zh: 若以諸君之力，得平關東，當以大義喻秦，奉迎反正。

translations.literal: If with your strength we can pacify the east of the Pass, I shall use righteousness to persuade Qin and welcome the return to the right path.
translations.idiomatic: If we pacify the east with your help, I will persuade Qin by righteousness and restore the throne.

sentences.zh: 無上自尊，非孤心也。

translations.literal: To exalt oneself without limit is not my heart.
translations.idiomatic: To seize the crown for myself is not my wish.

sentences.zh: 」謀於眾曰：「洛陽四面受敵，北阻大河，至於控馭燕、趙，非形勝之便，不如北取鄴都，據之而制天下。

translations.literal: He consulted the assembly: "Luoyang is attacked on four sides; northward the great river blocks the way; as for controlling Yan and Zhao, it lacks the advantage of commanding terrain—it is better to go north and take the capital at Ye, hold it, and master the realm."
translations.idiomatic: He told his officers, "Luoyang is beset on every side, with the Yellow River to the north. It is no strongpoint for ruling Yan and Zhao. Better march north, seize Ye, and command the realm from there."

sentences.zh: 」眾咸以為然。

translations.literal: The assembly all agreed.
translations.idiomatic: All agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃引師而東，遣建威將軍王騰起浮橋于石門。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led his army east and sent the general Wang Teng to build a pontoon bridge at Shimen.
translations.idiomatic: He marched east and sent Wang Teng to throw a pontoon bridge across at Shimen.

sentences.zh: 初，垂之發鄴中，子農及兄子楷、紹，北子宙，為苻丕所留。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chui set out from Ye, his son Nong and his brother's sons Kai and Shao, and his northern son Zhou, had been detained by Fu Pi.
translations.idiomatic: When Chui left Ye, Pi had held back his son Nong, his nephews Kai and Shao, and another son Zhou.

sentences.zh: 及誅飛龍，遣田生密告農等，使起兵趙、魏以相應。

translations.literal: After he executed Feilong, he sent Tian Sheng in secret to inform Nong and the others to raise troops in Zhao and Wei in coordination.
translations.idiomatic: After killing Feilong he sent Tian Sheng secretly to tell Nong and the others to rise in Zhao and Wei.

sentences.zh: 於是農、宙奔列人，楷、紹奔辟陽，眾咸應之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Nong and Zhou fled to Lieren, Kai and Shao to Piyang, and the masses all responded.
translations.idiomatic: Nong and Zhou fled to Lieren, Kai and Shao to Piyang, and the people rallied to them.

sentences.zh: 農西招庫辱官偉於上黨，東引乞特歸於東阿，各率眾數萬赴之，眾至十餘萬。

translations.literal: Nong summoned Guan Wei of the Kuru in Shangdang from the west and Qi Te Gui of the eastern tribes at Dong'e from the east; each led tens of thousands to join him until the host reached more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Nong called Guan Wei of the Kuru in the west and Qi Te Gui in the east; each brought tens of thousands until their force passed a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 丕遣石越討農，為農所敗，斬越于陳。

translations.literal: Pi sent Shi Yue to attack Nong; Nong defeated him and beheaded Yue at Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Pi sent Shi Yue against Nong. Nong routed him and killed Yue at Chen.

sentences.zh: 垂引兵至滎陽，乙太元八年自稱大將軍、大都督、燕王，承制行事，建元曰燕元。

translations.literal: Chui led his army to Xingyang; in the eighth year of the Taiyuan era he styled himself grand general, grand commander, and King of Yan, acting by imperial mandate, and established the reign title Yan Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: At Xingyang, in the eighth year of the Taiyuan era, Chui declared himself grand general, grand commander, and king of Yan, ruling by provisional mandate under the reign title Yan Yuan.

sentences.zh: 令稱統府，府置四佐，王公已下稱臣，凡所封拜，一如王者，以翟斌為建義大將軍，封河南王；

translations.literal: He ordered that his headquarters be called the supreme commandery, with four aides; kings and dukes and below addressed him as lord; all enfeoffments followed royal practice. He made Zhai Bin general who establishes righteousness and King of Henan;
translations.idiomatic: His headquarters was styled the supreme command; four aides were appointed; princes and ministers called him lord. Enfeoffments followed royal forms. Zhai Bin was made general who establishes righteousness and king of Henan;

sentences.zh: 翟檀為柱國大將軍、弘農王；

translations.literal: Zhai Tan was made pillar-of-state general and King of Hongnong;
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Tan became pillar-of-state general and king of Hongnong;

sentences.zh: 弟德為車騎大將軍、范陽王；

translations.literal: his younger brother De was made general of chariots and cavalry and King of Fanyang;
translations.idiomatic: his brother De was general of chariots and cavalry and king of Fanyang;

sentences.zh: 兄子楷征西大將軍、太原王。

translations.literal: his brother's son Kai was made general who campaigns west and King of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: his nephew Kai was general who campaigns west and king of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 眾至二十餘萬，濟自石門，長驅攻鄴。

translations.literal: His force reached more than two hundred thousand; crossing at Shimen, he drove at full speed to attack Ye.
translations.idiomatic: His army swelled past two hundred thousand. He crossed at Shimen and marched hard on Ye.

sentences.zh: 農、楷、紹、宙等率眾會垂。

translations.literal: Nong, Kai, Shao, Zhou, and the others led their troops to join Chui.
translations.idiomatic: Nong, Kai, Shao, Zhou, and the rest joined Chui with their hosts.

sentences.zh: 立子寶為燕王太子，封功臣為公侯伯子男者百餘人。

translations.literal: He established his son Bao as crown prince of Yan and enfeoffed more than a hundred meritorious ministers as dukes, marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons.
translations.idiomatic: He named Bao crown prince and enfeoffed over a hundred ministers as dukes, marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons.

sentences.zh: 苻丕乃遣侍郎姜讓謂垂曰：「往歲大駕失據，君保衛鑾輿，勤王誠義，邁蹤前烈。

translations.literal: Fu Pi then sent the attendant Jiang Rang to tell Chui: "In former years when the imperial carriage was lost, you guarded the sacred chariot and showed the utmost loyalty in coming to the sovereign's aid—your merit surpasses the heroes of old.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi sent Jiang Rang to Chui: "When the emperor fled disaster, you guarded him and served with surpassing loyalty.

sentences.zh: 宜述修前規，終忠貞之節，奈何棄崇山之功，為此過舉！

translations.literal: You ought to follow and renew your former course and keep to the end your loyal and steadfast integrity—why abandon the achievement of a towering mountain for this excessive act!
translations.idiomatic: Return to that path and keep faith to the end. Why throw away great merit for this rebellion?

sentences.zh: 過貴能改，先賢之嘉事也。

translations.literal: To correct a fault when one has gone too far is a fine thing praised by the sages of old.
translations.idiomatic: The sages praised those who amend their errors.

sentences.zh: 深宜詳思，悟猶未晚。

translations.literal: Think deeply on this—it is not too late to understand.
translations.idiomatic: Think on it. It is not too late.

sentences.zh: 」垂謂讓曰：「孤受主上不世之恩，故欲安全長樂公，使盡眾赴京師，然後修復家國之業，與秦永為鄰好。

translations.literal: Chui told Rang: "I received our sovereign's unexampled grace, and therefore wished to keep the Marquis of Changle safe, have him lead all his troops to the capital, and then restore the enterprise of house and state, remaining forever Qin's neighbor in friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Chui told Rang, "I owe the emperor boundless grace. I meant to see Fu Pi safely to the capital with all his troops, then restore Yan and remain Qin's friend.

sentences.zh: 何故暗於機運，不以鄴見歸也？

translations.literal: Why are you blind to the turn of fortune and will not surrender Ye to me?
translations.idiomatic: Why will you not read the times and yield Ye?

sentences.zh: 大義滅親，況于意氣之顧！

translations.literal: Righteousness may extinguish kinship—how much more a bond of personal favor!
translations.idiomatic: When righteousness demands it, kinship gives way—what of mere favor?

sentences.zh: 公若迷而不返者，孤亦欲竊兵勢耳。

translations.literal: If you are deluded and do not return, I too mean to take up military force.
translations.idiomatic: If you will not turn back, I will use force.

sentences.zh: 今事已然，恐單馬乞命不可得也。

translations.literal: Now that matters have come to this, I fear that begging for life on a single horse will not be possible.
translations.idiomatic: The matter is settled. Do not hope to beg your life alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 」讓厲色責垂曰：「將軍不容于家國，投命於聖朝，燕之尺土，將軍豈有分乎！

translations.literal: Rang sternly reproached Chui: "The general had no place in his house and state and cast his fate on the holy dynasty—of Yan's land inch by inch, does the general have any share!
translations.idiomatic: Rang rebuked him: "You had no place in Yan and came to Qin. What right have you to Yan's soil?

sentences.zh: 主上與將軍風殊類別，臭味不同，奇將軍于一見，托將軍以斷金，寵逾宗舊，任齊懿籓，自古君臣冥契之重，豈甚此邪！

translations.literal: Our sovereign and the general differ in wind and type, in taste and odor; yet in a single meeting he regarded the general as extraordinary, entrusted the general with a bond cut from metal, favored you beyond old kin, and charged you equal to the most honored of the frontier—since antiquity has the weight of such communion between lord and minister ever exceeded this!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor and you are not of one kind, yet he honored you at first sight, bound you as kin, favored you above old friends, and gave you rank equal to the greatest princes. Never was trust like this!

sentences.zh: 方付將軍以六尺之孤，萬里之命，奈何王師小敗，便有二圖！

translations.literal: He was about to entrust the six-foot orphan and the mandate of ten thousand li to you—why, at a small defeat of the royal army, do you now harbor two designs!
translations.idiomatic: He would have entrusted his son and the realm to you. Why, after one defeat, plot treason?

sentences.zh: 夫師起無名，終則弗成，天之所廢，人不能支。

translations.literal: When an army rises without a righteous name, in the end it cannot succeed; what Heaven abandons, men cannot support.
translations.idiomatic: Armies without just cause fail. What heaven casts off, men cannot uphold.

sentences.zh: 將軍起無名之師，而欲興天所廢，竊未見其可。

translations.literal: The general has raised an army without a name and wishes to revive what Heaven has cast down—I do not yet see how this can succeed.
translations.idiomatic: You raise a lawless host to revive a doomed house. I see no hope in it.

sentences.zh: 長樂公主上之元子，聲德邁于唐、衛，居陝東之任，為朝廷維城，其可束手輸將軍以百城之地！

translations.literal: The Princess of Changle is the sovereign's eldest son by the primary consort; his fame and virtue surpass Tang Shu and Wei Kang; he holds charge east of the Pass as the court's bulwark—how could he meekly hand the general a hundred cities!
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi is the heir, famed like the princes of Zhou, the court's shield in the east. He will not meekly yield you a hundred cities.

sentences.zh: 大夫死王事，國君死社稷，將軍欲裂冠毀冕，拔本塞源者，自可任將軍兵勢，何復多雲。

translations.literal: Great officers die for the king's affairs; the lord of the state dies for the altars. If the general wishes to tear the cap and destroy the regalia, uproot the source and block the flow, you may rely on your military might—why say more.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers die for their lord; rulers die for the altars. If you mean to rebel, use your armies. I have said enough.

sentences.zh: 但念將軍以七十之年，懸首白旗，高世之忠，忽為逆鬼，竊為將軍痛之。

translations.literal: Yet I think of the general at seventy years, hanging your head from a white flag—the loyalty of one who towers above his age suddenly become a rebellious ghost; I grieve for the general on your account.
translations.idiomatic: You are seventy. Think of your head on a pole—loyalty turned to treason. I grieve for you.

sentences.zh: 」垂默然。

translations.literal: Chui was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Chui said nothing.

sentences.zh: 左右勸垂殺之，垂曰：「古者兵交，使在其間，犬各吠非其主，何所問也！

translations.literal: Those about him urged Chui to kill him. Chui said: "In antiquity when armies met, envoys stood between them; dogs each bark at what is not their master—what is there to ask!
translations.idiomatic: His men urged death. Chui said, "When armies meet, envoys pass between them. Dogs bark at strangers. Why blame him?

sentences.zh: 」乃遣讓歸。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Rang back.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Rang away unharmed.

sentences.zh: 垂上表於苻堅曰：「臣才非古人，致禍起蕭牆，身嬰時難，歸命聖朝。

translations.literal: Chui submitted a memorial to Fu Jian saying: "My talent does not match the men of old; disaster arose within the palace walls; I myself met the hardship of the times and cast my fate on the holy dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Chui wrote to Fu Jian: "I am no sage of old. Trouble rose within my house. I came to you in my need.

sentences.zh: 陛下恩深周、漢，猥叨微顧之遇，位為列將，爵忝通侯，誓在戮力輸誠，常懼不及。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's grace is as deep as Zhou and Han; I have presumptuously received the favor of a slight regard, holding rank among the generals and sharing the title of full marquis, vowing to exert my strength and offer loyalty, ever fearing I fall short.
translations.idiomatic: Your grace equals Zhou and Han. You made me a general and a marquis. I swore to serve with all my strength.

sentences.zh: 去夏桓沖送死，一擬雲消，回討鄖城，俘馘萬計，斯誠陛下神算之奇，頗亦愚臣忘死之效。

translations.literal: Last summer Huan Chong came to his death; in one stroke clouds dispersed; returning to attack Yuncheng, captives and severed ears numbered in the tens of thousands—this was truly the marvel of Your Majesty's divine calculation, and also in part the effect of this foolish minister's forgetting death.
translations.idiomatic: Last summer we shattered Huan Chong. At Yuncheng we took tens of thousands. That was your divine strategy—and my willingness to die for you.

sentences.zh: 方將飲馬桂州，懸旌閩會，不圖天助亂德，大駕班師。

translations.literal: I was about to water our horses at Guizhou and hang our banners at Min and Yue, when unexpectedly Heaven aided disorderly virtue and the imperial carriage withdrew its ranks.
translations.idiomatic: I meant to drive to Guilin and plant banners in Fujian. Then heaven aided Qin's enemies and the great host retreated.

sentences.zh: 陛下單馬奔臣，臣奉衛匪貳，豈陛下聖明鑒臣單心，皇天后土實亦知之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty came on a single horse to me; I received and guarded you without disloyalty—surely Your Majesty in sagely discernment sees my single heart; the August Lord on High and Earth below truly know it as well.
translations.idiomatic: You fled to me alone on horseback. I guarded you without wavering. Heaven and earth know my heart.

sentences.zh: 臣奉詔北巡，受制長樂。

translations.literal: I received the edict to tour north and was placed under the Marquis of Changle's command.
translations.idiomatic: I was ordered north under Fu Pi's command.

sentences.zh: 然丕外失眾心，內多猜忌，今臣野次外庭，不聽謁廟。

translations.literal: Yet Pi outwardly lost the hearts of the masses and inwardly harbored many suspicions; now I camp in the outer court and am not permitted to pay respects at the temple.
translations.idiomatic: Pi lost the people's hearts and trusts no one. I camp outside the walls and may not enter the shrine.

sentences.zh: 丁零逆豎寇逼豫州，丕迫臣單赴，限以師程，惟給弊卒二千，盡無兵杖，復令飛龍潛為刺客。

translations.literal: The Dingling rebel pressed Yuzhou; Pi forced me to go alone, setting a deadline on the campaign, giving only two thousand worn troops without weapons, and again set Feilong secretly as assassin.
translations.idiomatic: The Dingling pressed Yuzhou. Pi sent me with two thousand broken men, no arms, and Feilong to murder me in secret.

sentences.zh: 及至洛陽，平原公暉復不信納。

translations.literal: When I reached Luoyang, the Duke of Pingyuan Hui again would not trust or accept me.
translations.idiomatic: At Luoyang, Fu Hui would not admit me.

sentences.zh: 臣竊惟進無淮陰功高之慮，退無李廣失利之愆，懼有青蠅，交亂白黑，丁零夷夏以臣忠而見疑，乃推臣為盟主。

translations.literal: I reflected that advancing I lacked the worry of Huaiyin's too-high merit, and retreating I lacked Li Guang's fault of defeat—yet I feared green flies would mingle and confuse black and white; the Dingling, barbarian and Chinese alike, because I was loyal yet suspected, thereupon urged me as league chief.
translations.idiomatic: I had neither Han Xin's fear of too great merit nor Li Guang's disgrace in retreat. Yet slander might confuse truth. Barbarian and Chinese alike, seeing my loyalty doubted, made me their leader.

sentences.zh: 臣受託善始，不遂令終，泣望西京，揮涕即邁。

translations.literal: I received the trust at a good beginning but cannot bring it to a good end; weeping I gaze toward the western capital and, brushing away tears, set out.
translations.idiomatic: Trusted at the start, I cannot end well. Weeping I turn from the western capital and march away.

sentences.zh: 軍次石門，所在雲赴，雖復周武之會于孟津，漢祖之集於垓下，不期之眾，實有甚焉。

translations.literal: When the army halted at Shimen, from every place clouds of men came—though it recalls King Wu's gathering at Mengjin and Han Gaozu's assembly at Gaixia, the unexpected host in truth greatly exceeded them.
translations.idiomatic: At Shimen men gathered like clouds—a host greater than King Wu at Mengjin or Liu Bang at Gaixia.

sentences.zh: 欲令長樂公盡眾赴難，以禮發遣，而丕固守匹夫之志，不達變通之理。

translations.literal: I wished to have the Marquis of Changle lead all his troops to the difficulty and send them off with ceremony, but Pi clung to the will of a common fellow and did not comprehend the principle of adapting to change.
translations.idiomatic: I asked Fu Pi to march out with all his men. He clung to obstinacy and would not bend.

sentences.zh: 臣息農收集故營，以備不虞，而石越傾鄴城之眾，輕相掩襲，兵陣未交，越已隕首。

translations.literal: My son Nong gathered the old camps to guard against the unforeseen, yet Shi Yue led the masses of Ye city in a light surprise attack; before the battle lines met, Yue had already lost his head.
translations.idiomatic: My son Nong rallied old camps for defense. Shi Yue led Ye's host against him and was killed before battle was joined.

sentences.zh: 臣既單車懸軫，歸者如雲，斯實天符，非臣之力。

translations.literal: I then came with a single carriage and hanging reins, and those who returned came like clouds—this was truly Heaven's talisman, not my strength.
translations.idiomatic: I came alone, and men flocked to me like clouds. That was heaven's sign, not my power.

sentences.zh: 且鄴者臣國舊都，應即惠及，然後西面受制，永守東籓，上成陛下遇臣之意，下全愚臣感報之誠。

translations.literal: Moreover Ye is my state's former capital and ought to receive favor at once; then, submitting to command from the west, I would forever guard the eastern frontier—above fulfilling Your Majesty's intent in treating me, below completing this foolish minister's portion of repaying kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Ye is my old capital. Grant it to me, and I will serve you from the east forever—fulfilling your grace and my debt.

sentences.zh: 今進師圍鄴，並喻丕以天時人事。

translations.literal: Now I advance the army to besiege Ye and have informed Pi of both Heaven's season and human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Now I besiege Ye and have told Pi what heaven and duty demand.

sentences.zh: 而丕不察機運，杜門自守，時出挑戰，鋒戈屢交，恆恐飛矢誤中，以傷陛下天性之念。

translations.literal: Yet Pi does not discern the turn of fortune, shuts his gates and holds defense, and from time to time comes out to challenge; blades and spears have crossed repeatedly, and I constantly fear a stray arrow may strike by mistake and wound Your Majesty's natural feeling of kinship.
translations.idiomatic: Pi will not yield. He sallies to fight again and again. I fear a stray shaft may wound your fatherly heart.

sentences.zh: 臣之此誠，未簡神聽，輒遏兵止銳，不敢竊攻。

translations.literal: This sincerity of mine has not yet reached divine hearing; I therefore hold the army and blunt its edge and dare not attack in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has not heard me. I hold my troops and dare not strike in secret.

sentences.zh: 夫運有推移，去來常事，惟陛下察之。」

translations.literal: Fortune has its shifts; coming and going are ordinary matters—may Your Majesty discern this."
translations.idiomatic: Fortune turns. Coming and going are the way of things. May Your Majesty see it."

sentences.zh: 堅報曰：「朕以不德，忝承靈命，君臨萬邦，三十年矣。

translations.literal: Jian replied: "I, lacking virtue, have presumptuously received the numinous mandate and ruled ten thousand states for thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: Jian answered: "Lacking virtue, I have ruled thirty years by heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 遐方幽裔，莫不來庭，惟東南一隅，敢違王命。

translations.literal: Remote lands and distant tribes have all come to court; only in the southeast corner do they dare defy the royal command.
translations.idiomatic: All the world has submitted save the southeast, which still defies me.

sentences.zh: 朕爰奮六師，恭行天罰，而玄機不吊，王師敗績。

translations.literal: I therefore roused the six armies and respectfully executed Heaven's punishment, yet the mysterious principle did not aid me and the royal army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: I marched the six hosts to punish them, but heaven did not aid me and my army was broken.

sentences.zh: 賴卿忠誠之至，輔翼朕躬，社稷之不隕，卿之力也。

translations.literal: Relying on your utmost loyalty in assisting and supporting my person, that the altars did not fall is your strength.
translations.idiomatic: You saved me at Feishui. The altars stand because of you.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：『中心藏之，何日忘之。

translations.literal: The Odes say: "Hidden in the center—what day shall I forget it."
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say, "I hide it in my heart—when shall I forget?"

sentences.zh: 』方任卿以元相，爵卿以郡侯，庶弘濟艱難，敬酬勳烈，何圖伯夷忽毀冰操，柳惠倏為淫夫！

translations.literal: I was about to charge you as chief minister and enfeoff you Marquis of a commandery, hoping broadly to relieve difficulty and respectfully repay meritorious achievement—who imagined that Bo Yi would suddenly destroy his icy integrity, or that Liu Xia Hui would abruptly become a debauchee!
translations.idiomatic: I meant to make you chief minister and a marquis, to share hardship and honor your deeds. Who thought Bo Yi would break his vow, or Liu Xia Hui turn lecher?

sentences.zh: 覽表惋然，有慚朝士。

translations.literal: Reading your memorial, I am grieved and ashamed before the court gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Your letter grieves and shames me before the court.

sentences.zh: 卿既不容於本朝，匹馬而投命，朕則寵卿以將位，禮卿以上賓，任同舊臣，爵齊勳輔，歃血斷金，披心相付。

translations.literal: You had no place in your native court; on a single horse you came to entrust your life. I then favored you with the rank of general and treated you as a supreme guest, charging you equal to old ministers and enfeoffing you equal to meritorious assistants—we drank blood and cut metal and opened our hearts to one another.
translations.idiomatic: Cast out from Yan, you came to me on one horse. I made you a great general and honored guest, equal to my oldest ministers. We swore blood brotherhood and opened our hearts.

sentences.zh: 謂卿食椹懷音，保之偕老。

translations.literal: I said you would, eating mulberries, cherish the old tune and keep faith to old age.
translations.idiomatic: I thought you would keep faith to the end, like the man who, eating mulberries, remembered home.

sentences.zh: 豈意畜水覆舟，養獸反害，悔之噬臍，將何所及！

translations.literal: Who imagined that water would overturn the boat and reared beasts would turn to harm—regret bites to the navel; what is there to reach!
translations.idiomatic: Who thought the boat you filled would sink you, the beast you fed would bite you? Regret comes too late.

sentences.zh: 誕言駭眾，誇擬非常，周武之事，豈卿庸人所可論哉！

translations.literal: Wild words frighten the masses; boasting compares to what is extraordinary—the affairs of King Wu of Zhou—how can such things be discussed by a mediocrity like you!
translations.idiomatic: Your boasts terrify men and ape King Wu. Such things are not for the likes of you.

sentences.zh: 失籠之鳥，非羅所羈；

translations.literal: A bird escaped its cage is not held by any net;
translations.idiomatic: A bird out of the cage escapes every net;

sentences.zh: 脫網之鯨，豈罟所制！

translations.literal: a whale off the net—how can a seine control it!
translations.idiomatic: a whale free of the seine breaks every trap.

sentences.zh: 翹陸任懷，何須聞也。

translations.literal: Whether you leap on land or swim in water, take your will—why need I hear of it.
translations.idiomatic: Go where you will on land or water. I need not hear more.

sentences.zh: 念卿垂老，老而為賊，生為叛臣，死為逆鬼，侏張幽顯，布毒存亡，中原士女，何痛如之！

translations.literal: Thinking of you in old age, old yet becoming a bandit—alive a rebellious minister, dead a rebellious ghost—you stretch your limbs through hidden and manifest realms and spread poison through the living and dead; the gentlemen and ladies of the central plains—what pain like this!
translations.idiomatic: Old man, you choose to be a rebel in your age—traitor in life, outcast in death, poisoning land and people. What pain for the heartland!

sentences.zh: 朕之曆運興喪，豈復由卿！

translations.literal: Whether my dynasty's fortune rises or falls—how could that again depend on you!
translations.idiomatic: Whether my house stands or falls does not depend on you.

sentences.zh: 但長樂、平原以未立之年，遇卿於兩都，慮其經略未稱朕心，所恨者此焉而已。」

translations.literal: Only the Marquis of Changle and the Duke of Pingyuan, in years not yet established, met you in the two capitals—I fear their planning did not match my heart; this alone is my regret."
translations.idiomatic: Only Fu Pi and Fu Hui, still young when they knew you in the capitals, may lack judgment. That alone I regret."

sentences.zh: 垂攻拔鄴郛，丕固守中城，垂塹而圍之，分遣老弱于魏郡、肥鄉，築新興城以置輜重，擁漳水以灌之。

translations.literal: Chui stormed and took the outer wall of Ye; Pi firmly held the inner city. Chui moated and besieged it, sent the old and weak to Wei commandery and Feixiang, built Xinxing city to store baggage, and dammed the Zhang River to flood it.
translations.idiomatic: Chui took Ye's outer walls. Pi held the inner city. Chui dug moats, moved supplies to Xinxing, and dammed the Zhang to flood the town.

sentences.zh: 翟斌潛諷丁零及西人，請斌為尚書令。

translations.literal: Zhai Bin secretly incited the Dingling and westerners to ask that Bin be made director of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Bin secretly urged the Dingling and western troops to demand he be made chief minister.

sentences.zh: 垂訪之群僚，其安東將軍封衡厲色曰：「馬能千里，不免羈靽，明畜生不可以人禦也。

translations.literal: Chui consulted the officials; his general Feng Heng of Andong said with stern countenance: "A horse may run a thousand li but cannot escape the bridle; bright beasts cannot be ruled by men.
translations.idiomatic: Chui asked his officers. Feng Heng said sharply, "A horse may run a thousand li but needs the bridle. A bright beast cannot be ruled like a man.

sentences.zh: 斌戎狄小人，遭時際會，兄弟封王，自驩兜已來，未有此福。

translations.literal: Bin is a barbarian petty man who met the fortune of the times; his brothers were enfeoffed kings—from Huan Dou down there has been no such blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Bin is a barbarian who rose by chance. His kin became kings—since antiquity, none were so favored.

sentences.zh: 忽履盈忘止，復有斯求，魂爽錯亂，必死不出年也。

translations.literal: Suddenly treading fullness he forgets to stop and again makes this demand—his soul is disordered; he will surely die within the year.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk on fortune, he asks for more. His soul is lost. He will not live out the year.

sentences.zh: 」垂猶隱忍容之，令曰：「翟王之功宜居上輔，但台既未建，此官不可便置。

translations.literal: Chui still concealed his anger and tolerated him, issuing an order: "Prince Zhai's achievement ought to occupy the highest assistant post, but since the terrace is not yet built, this office cannot be set at once.
translations.idiomatic: Chui hid his anger and said, "Prince Zhai deserves the highest post, but the government is not yet established. Wait.

sentences.zh: 待六合廓清，更當議之。

translations.literal: When the six directions are cleared, we shall discuss it again."
translations.idiomatic: When the realm is pacified, we will speak of it again."

sentences.zh: 」斌怒，密應苻丕，潛使丁零決防潰水。

translations.literal: Bin grew angry and secretly responded to Fu Pi, secretly causing the Dingling to break the dike and release the flood.
translations.idiomatic: Bin in secret allied with Fu Pi and had the Dingling breach the dike.

sentences.zh: 事泄，垂誅之。

translations.literal: When the matter was exposed, Chui executed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was found out, Chui killed him.

sentences.zh: 斌兄子真率其部眾北走邯鄲，引兵向鄴，欲與丕為內外之勢，垂令其太子寶、冠軍慕容隆擊破之。

translations.literal: Bin's nephew Zhen led his tribal force north to Handan and turned his army toward Ye, intending to coordinate with Pi inside and outside; Chui ordered his crown prince Bao and the champion Murong Long to defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Bin's nephew Zhen fled north to Handan and marched on Ye to aid Pi within the walls. Chui sent Bao and Murong Long to break him.

sentences.zh: 真自邯鄲北走，又使慕容楷率騎追之，戰於下邑，為真所敗，真遂屯于承營。

translations.literal: Zhen fled north from Handan; Chui again sent Murong Kai with cavalry in pursuit; they fought at Xiayi and Kai was defeated by Zhen; Zhen then encamped at Chengying.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen fled from Handan. Chui sent Murong Kai after him. Kai was beaten at Xiayi. Zhen camped at Chengying.

sentences.zh: 垂謂諸將曰：「苻丕窮寇，必守死不降。

translations.literal: Chui told the generals: "Fu Pi is a cornered foe and will surely hold to death and not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Chui told his generals, "Fu Pi is trapped. He will die before he yields.

sentences.zh: 丁零叛擾，乃我腹心之患。

translations.literal: The Dingling in rebellion and disorder are the trouble of our heart and belly.
translations.idiomatic: The rebellious Dingling are the wound in our belly.

sentences.zh: 吾欲遷師新城，開其逸路，進以謝秦主疇昔之恩，退以嚴擊真之備。

translations.literal: I wish to move the army to Xincheng, open a path of escape for them, advance to repay the Qin sovereign's grace of former days, and retire to strike hard at Zhen's preparations."
translations.idiomatic: I will move to Xincheng, leave Pi a way out, repay Qin's old kindness, and turn to crush Zhen."

sentences.zh: 」於是引師去鄴，北屯新城。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led his army away from Ye and encamped north at Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew from Ye and camped north at Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 慕容農進攻翟嵩于黃泥，破之。

translations.literal: Murong Nong advanced to attack Zhai Song at Huangni and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Nong attacked Zhai Song at Huangni and routed him.

sentences.zh: 垂謂其范陽王德曰：「苻丕吾縱之不能去，方引晉師規固鄴都，不可置也。

translations.literal: Chui told his Prince of Fanyang De: "Fu Pi—I let him go and he would not leave; now he is bringing Jin armies to try to hold Ye—I cannot leave him in place."
translations.idiomatic: Chui told Murong De, "I spared Fu Pi and he would not go. Now he calls in Jin to hold Ye. I cannot leave him there."

sentences.zh: 」進師又攻鄴，開其西奔之路。

translations.literal: He advanced the army again to attack Ye and opened a western route for flight.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on Ye again and opened the western gate for Pi to flee.

sentences.zh: 垂將有北都中山之意，農率眾數萬迎之。

translations.literal: Chui intended to make Zhongshan his northern capital; Nong led tens of thousands to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Chui meant to establish his northern capital at Zhongshan. Nong led tens of thousands out to meet him.

sentences.zh: 群僚聞慕容暐為苻堅所殺，勸垂僭位。

translations.literal: When the officials heard that Murong Wei had been killed by Fu Jian, they urged Chui to presumptuously take the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Murong Wei had been killed by Fu Jian, his officers urged him to declare himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 垂以慕容沖稱號關中，不許。

translations.literal: Chui, because Murong Chong had assumed a title in the Guanzhong region, did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chong had already claimed the throne in Guanzhong, so Chui refused.

sentences.zh: 晉龍驤將軍劉牢之率眾救苻丕，至鄴，垂逆戰，敗績，遂撤鄴圍，退屯新城。

translations.literal: The Jin general Liu Laozhi of the soaring dragon led troops to rescue Fu Pi; when he reached Ye, Chui met him in battle and was defeated, whereupon he lifted the siege of Ye and withdrew to encamp at Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Laozhi of Jin marched to relieve Fu Pi. Chui met him at Ye, was beaten, lifted the siege, and fell back to Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 垂自新城北走，牢之追垂，連戰皆敗。

translations.literal: Chui fled north from Xincheng; Laozhi pursued Chui and in successive battles all were defeats.
translations.idiomatic: Chui fled north from Xincheng. Laozhi pursued him and won every clash.

sentences.zh: 又戰於五橋澤，王師敗績，德及隆引兵要之於五丈橋，牢之馳馬跳五丈澗，會苻丕救至而免。

translations.literal: They fought again at the marshes of Wuqiao; the royal army was defeated. De and Long led troops to intercept at Wuzhang Bridge; Laozhi spurred his horse and leaped the Wuzhang ravine, and when Fu Pi's rescue arrived he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuqiao marshes Chui's army broke. De and Long blocked Wuzhang Bridge. Laozhi leaped the ravine and escaped when Fu Pi's relief arrived.

sentences.zh: 翟真去承營，徙屯行唐，真司馬鮮于乞殺真，盡誅翟氏，自立為趙王。

translations.literal: Zhai Zhen left Chengying and moved his camp to Xingtang; Zhen's chief clerk Xianyu Qi killed Zhen, executed the entire Zhai clan, and set himself up as King of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Zhen left Chengying for Xingtang. His clerk Xianyu Qi murdered him, wiped out the Zhai house, and declared himself king of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 營人攻殺乞，迎立真從弟成為主，真子遼奔黎陽。

translations.literal: The camp soldiers attacked and killed Qi and welcomed Zhen's cousin Cheng as lord; Zhen's son Liao fled to Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: The troops killed Qi and made Zhen's cousin Cheng leader. Zhen's son Liao fled to Liyang.

sentences.zh: 高句驪寇遼東，垂平北慕容佐遣司馬郝景率眾救之，為高句驪所敗，遼東、玄菟遂沒。

translations.literal: Koguryo raided Liaodong; Murong Zuo the pacifier of the north sent the marshal Hao Jing with troops to rescue, but was defeated by Koguryo, and Liaodong and Xuantu were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Koguryo raided Liaodong. Murong Zuo sent Hao Jing to relieve the province but was routed. Liaodong and Xuantu fell.

sentences.zh: 建節將軍徐岩叛于武邑，驅掠四千餘人，北走幽州。

translations.literal: The general who establishes authority Xu Yan rebelled at Wuyi, drove off and plundered more than four thousand people, and fled north toward Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yan rebelled at Wuyi, seized more than four thousand people, and fled north toward Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 垂馳敕其將平規曰：「但固守勿戰，比破丁零，吾當自討之。

translations.literal: Chui sent a rapid order to his general Ping Gui: "Only hold firm and do not fight; after I break the Dingling I shall come myself to punish him."
translations.idiomatic: Chui ordered Ping Gui, "Hold your ground and do not fight. When I have broken the Dingling I will come myself."

sentences.zh: 」規違命距戰，為岩所敗。

translations.literal: Gui disobeyed the command and met in battle; he was defeated by Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Gui disobeyed, gave battle, and was beaten.

sentences.zh: 岩乘勝入薊，掠千餘戶而去，所過寇暴，遂據令支。

translations.literal: Yan pressed his victory into Ji, plundered more than a thousand households and left; wherever he passed he raided and ravaged, and then occupied Lingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yan stormed Ji, looted a thousand households, and ravaged the countryside before seizing Lingzhi.

sentences.zh: 翟成長史鮮于得斬成而降，垂入行唐，悉坑其眾。

translations.literal: Cheng's chief clerk Xianyu De beheaded Cheng and surrendered; Chui entered Xingtang and buried alive all his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng's clerk Xianyu De killed him and surrendered. Chui entered Xingtang and massacred the garrison.

sentences.zh: 苻丕棄鄴城，奔於并州。

translations.literal: Fu Pi abandoned Ye city and fled to Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Pi abandoned Ye and fled to Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 慕容農攻克令支，斬徐岩兄弟。

translations.literal: Murong Nong stormed and took Lingzhi and beheaded Xu Yan and his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Nong took Lingzhi and executed Xu Yan and his brothers.

sentences.zh: 時伐高句驪，復遼東、玄菟二郡，還屯龍城。

translations.literal: At that time he campaigned against Koguryo, recovered the two commanderies of Liaodong and Xuantu, and returned to encamp at Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned against Koguryo, recovered Liaodong and Xuantu, and returned to Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 遣其征西慕容楷、衛軍慕容麟、鎮南慕容紹、征虜慕容宙等攻苻堅冀州牧苻定、鎮東苻紹、幽州牧苻謨、鎮北苻亮。

translations.literal: He sent his general who campaigns west Murong Kai, guard Murong Lin, pacifier of the south Murong Shao, and general who campaigns against barbarians Murong Zhou and others to attack Fu Jian's governors of Ji Province Fu Ding, pacifier of the east Fu Shao, governor of You Province Fu Mo, and pacifier of the north Fu Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Murong Kai, Murong Lin, Murong Shao, and Murong Zhou against Fu Jian's governors Fu Ding, Fu Shao, Fu Mo, and Fu Liang.

sentences.zh: 楷與定等書，喻以禍福，定等悉降。

translations.literal: Kai wrote to Ding and the others, explaining fortune and disaster, and Ding and the others all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Kai wrote to them of fortune and ruin. They all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 垂留其太子寶守中山，率諸將南攻翟遼，以楷為前鋒都督。

translations.literal: Chui left his crown prince Bao to guard Zhongshan and led the generals south to attack Zhai Liao, making Kai commander of the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Chui left Bao at Zhongshan and marched south against Zhai Liao with Kai as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 遼之部眾皆燕、趙人也，咸曰：「太原王之子，吾之父母。

translations.literal: Liao's tribal force were all men of Yan and Zhao and said: "The son of the Prince of Taiyuan is our father and mother."
translations.idiomatic: Liao's men were Yan and Zhao folk. They said, "The Prince of Taiyuan's son is our parent."

sentences.zh: 」相率歸附。

translations.literal: They came over to join him in succession.
translations.idiomatic: They defected to Kai in droves.

sentences.zh: 遼懼，遣使請降。

translations.literal: Liao was afraid and sent envoys to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Liao sent envoys to surrender.

sentences.zh: 垂至黎陽，遼肉袒謝罪，垂厚撫之。

translations.literal: When Chui reached Liyang, Liao bared his torso to confess guilt; Chui treated him with great kindness.
translations.idiomatic: At Liyang, Liao bared his chest in submission. Chui treated him generously.

sentences.zh: 為其太子寶起承華觀，以寶錄尚書政事，巨細皆委之，重總大綱而已。

translations.literal: He built the Chenghua terrace for his crown prince Bao, had Bao record the affairs of the masters of writing, entrusted great and small matters to him, and himself only grasped the great outline.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Chenghua terrace for Bao, put him in charge of the secretariat, and kept only the broad lines of policy himself.

sentences.zh: 立其夫人段氏為皇后。

translations.literal: He established his consort Lady Duan as empress.
translations.idiomatic: He made Lady Duan empress.

sentences.zh: 又以寶領侍中、大單于、驃騎大將軍、幽州牧。

translations.literal: He also made Bao concurrently palace attendant, great chanyu, general of agile cavalry, and governor of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was also made palace attendant, great chanyu, general of agile cavalry, and governor of You.

sentences.zh: 建留台于龍城，以高陽王慕容隆錄留台尚書事。

translations.literal: He established a rear capital at Longcheng and made the Prince of Gaoyang Murong Long recorder of the rear capital's masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: He set up a rear capital at Longcheng and made Murong Long its chief minister.

sentences.zh: 時慕容暐及諸宗室為苻堅所害者，並招魂葬之。

translations.literal: At that time Murong Wei and the various members of the imperial clan who had been killed by Fu Jian were all summoned in spirit and buried.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Wei and the royal dead slain by Fu Jian were given memorial burials by summoning their spirits.

sentences.zh: 清河太守賀耕聚眾定陵以叛，南應翟遼，慕容農討斬之，毀定陵城。

translations.literal: The governor of Qinghe He Geng gathered troops at Dingling to rebel, responding to Zhai Liao in the south; Murong Nong attacked and beheaded him and destroyed Dingling city.
translations.idiomatic: He Geng of Qinghe rebelled at Dingling and aided Zhai Liao. Murong Nong killed him and razed the town.

sentences.zh: 進師入鄴，以鄴城廣難固，築鳳陽門大道之東為隔城。

translations.literal: He advanced his army into Ye; because Ye city was broad and hard to defend, he built an inner city east of the Fengyang Gate avenue.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Ye. The city was too vast to hold, so he built an inner ward east of the Fengyang Gate road.

sentences.zh: 其尚書郎婁會上疏曰：「三年之喪，天下之達制，兵荒殺禮，遂以一切取士。

translations.literal: His master of writing Lang Lou Hui submitted a memorial saying: "The three-year mourning is the universal standard of the realm; in arms and famine rites of mourning were killed, and men were taken for office by every expedient.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Hui memorialized: "Three years' mourning is the universal norm. War and famine killed that rite, and office was filled by any means.

sentences.zh: 人心奔兢，苟求榮進，至乃身冒縗絰，以赴時役，豈必殉忠於國家，亦昧利於其間也。

translations.literal: Hearts race in competition, men seek advancement in haste, until some even wear hemp mourning to rush into seasonal service—not necessarily dying for loyalty to the state, but also blind to profit in the interval.
translations.idiomatic: Men scramble for rank, some even wearing mourning garb to take post—not from loyalty but from greed.

sentences.zh: 聖王設教，不以顛沛而虧其道，不以喪亂而變其化，故能杜豪兢之門，塞奔波之路。

translations.literal: The sage kings established teaching and did not let distress impair their Way, nor change their transformation because of mourning and disorder—thereby they could block the gate of fierce competition and dam the road of rushing about.
translations.idiomatic: The sages did not let hardship break the rites or chaos change the teaching. Thus they closed the door to reckless ambition.

sentences.zh: 陛下鐘百王之季，廓中興之業，天下漸平，兵革方偃，誠宜蠲蕩瑕穢，率由舊章。

translations.literal: Your Majesty tolls at the end of the hundred kings, expanding the enterprise of restoration; the realm is gradually pacified and arms are being laid aside—it is truly fitting to wash away flaws and follow the old statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty restores the dynasty amid ruin. The realm grows calm. It is time to cleanse abuses and restore the old rules.

sentences.zh: 吏遭大喪，聽終三年之禮，則四方知化，人斯服禮。

translations.literal: If officials who meet great bereavement are permitted to complete the three-year rites, then the four quarters will know transformation and men will submit to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Let officials observe three years' mourning for parents, and the realm will learn ritual again.

sentences.zh: 」垂不從。

translations.literal: Chui did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Chui refused.

sentences.zh: 翟遼死，子釗代立，攻逼鄴城，慕容農擊走之。

translations.literal: When Zhai Liao died, his son Zhao succeeded him, pressed Ye city, and Murong Nong drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Liao died. His son Zhao attacked Ye. Murong Nong repulsed him.

sentences.zh: 垂引師伐釗於滑台，次於黎陽津，釗于南岸距守，諸將惡其兵精，咸諫不宜濟河。

translations.literal: Chui led his army to campaign against Zhao at Huatai and halted at the Liyang ford; Zhao held the south bank in defense. The generals hated the excellence of his troops and all remonstrated that crossing the river was inadvisable.
translations.idiomatic: Chui marched on Zhao at Huatai and camped at Liyang ford. Zhao held the south bank. His officers feared Zhao's veterans and urged him not to cross.

sentences.zh: 垂笑曰：「堅子何能為，吾今為鯽等殺之。

translations.literal: Chui laughed and said: "What can that stripling do—I shall kill him for you carp today."
translations.idiomatic: Chui laughed. "What can that boy do? I will kill him for you today."

sentences.zh: 」遂徙營就西津，為牛皮船百餘艘，載疑兵列杖，溯流而上。

translations.literal: Thereupon he moved camp to the western ford, made more than a hundred boats of oxhide, loaded dummy troops with weapons displayed, and went upstream.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to the western ford, built a hundred oxhide boats loaded with dummy troops bearing arms, and sent them upstream.

sentences.zh: 釗先以大眾備黎陽，見垂向西津，乃棄營西距。

translations.literal: Zhao had first prepared a great host at Liyang; seeing Chui go to the western ford, he abandoned his camp and moved west to block.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao had massed at Liyang. Seeing Chui at the western ford, he marched west to meet him.

sentences.zh: 垂潛遣其桂林王慕容鎮、驃騎慕容國于黎陽津夜濟，壁于河南。

translations.literal: Chui secretly sent his Prince of Guilin Murong Zhen and general of agile cavalry Murong Guo to cross at the Liyang ford by night and build walls south of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Chui secretly sent Murong Zhen and Murong Guo to cross at Liyang by night and fortify the south bank.

sentences.zh: 釗聞而奔還，士眾疲渴，走歸滑台，釗攜妻子率數百騎北趣白鹿山。

translations.literal: When Zhao heard he hurried back; his troops were weary and thirsty and fled to Huatai; Zhao took wife and children and with several hundred horsemen fled north toward Bailu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao turned back exhausted. His men fled to Huatai. Zhao took his family and hundreds of horsemen toward Bailu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 農追擊，盡擒其眾，釗單騎奔長子。

translations.literal: Nong pursued, captured his entire force, and Zhao alone on horseback fled to Changzi.
translations.idiomatic: Nong pursued and took them all. Zhao alone escaped to Changzi.

sentences.zh: 釗所統七郡戶三萬八千皆安堵如故。

translations.literal: The seven commanderies under Zhao's rule, thirty-eight thousand households, were all settled in peace as before.
translations.idiomatic: The seven commanderies, thirty-eight thousand households, were left undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 徙徐州流人七千餘戶于黎陽。

translations.literal: He moved more than seven thousand displaced households of Xuzhou to Liyang.
