translations.idiomatic: More than seven thousand refugee families from Xuzhou were resettled at Liyang.

sentences.zh: 於是議征長子。

translations.literal: Thereupon they deliberated campaigning against Changzi.
translations.idiomatic: They debated an expedition against Changzi.

sentences.zh: 諸將咸諫，以慕容永未有釁，連歲征役，士卒疲怠，請俟他年。

translations.literal: The generals all remonstrated that Murong Yong had not yet given cause, that year after year of campaigns had worn out the troops, and asked to wait for another year.
translations.idiomatic: His officers urged delay. Murong Yong had given no opening; the army was weary after years of war.

sentences.zh: 垂將從之，及聞慕容德之策，笑曰：「吾計決矣。

translations.literal: Chui was about to follow them when he heard Murong De's plan and laughed: "My mind is made up.
translations.idiomatic: Chui was about to agree when he heard Murong De's counsel and laughed, "My mind is made.

sentences.zh: 且吾投老，扣囊底智，足以克之，不復留逆賊以累子孫也。

translations.literal: Moreover I am old; tapping the wisdom at the bottom of the bag is enough to overcome him—I will not leave rebellious bandits to burden my descendants."
translations.idiomatic: I am old, but the last wit in my bag is enough to crush him. I will not leave this rebel for my sons to fight."

sentences.zh: 」乃發步騎七萬，遣其丹陽王慕容贊、龍驤張崇攻永弟支于晉陽。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent seventy thousand foot and horse, dispatching his Prince of Danyang Murong Zan and soaring dragon Zhang Chong to attack Yong's younger brother Zhi at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: He marched seventy thousand foot and horse, sending Murong Zan and Zhang Chong against Yong's brother Zhi at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 永遣其將刁雲、慕容鐘率眾五萬屯潞川。

translations.literal: Yong sent his generals Diao Yun and Murong Zhong with fifty thousand troops to camp at Luchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yong sent Diao Yun and Murong Zhong with fifty thousand men to Luchuan.

sentences.zh: 垂遣慕容楷出自滏口，慕容農入自壺關，垂頓於鄴之西南，月餘不進。

translations.literal: Chui sent Murong Kai out from Fukou and Murong Nong in from Huguan; Chui himself halted southwest of Ye and for more than a month did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Kai marched from Fukou, Nong from Huguan. Chui camped southwest of Ye and did not move for a month.

sentences.zh: 永謂垂詭道伐之，乃攝諸軍還杜太行軹關。

translations.literal: Yong thought Chui was using a feint and would attack elsewhere; he therefore gathered all armies back to guard the Zhihang Pass of the Taihang Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Yong thought it a feint and pulled his armies back to guard Zhihang Pass in the Taihang.

sentences.zh: 垂進師入自天井關，至於壺壁。

translations.literal: Chui advanced through Tianjing Pass and reached Hubi.
translations.idiomatic: Chui marched through Tianjing Pass to Hubi.

sentences.zh: 永率精卒五萬來距，阻河曲以自固，馳使請戰。

translations.literal: Yong led fifty thousand picked troops to resist, blocked the river bend to secure himself, and sent a swift messenger to request battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yong came with fifty thousand elite troops, blocked the river bend, and challenged him to fight.

sentences.zh: 垂列陣於壺避之南，農、楷分為二翼，慕容國伏千兵於深澗，與永大戰。

translations.literal: Chui drew up battle lines south of Hubi; Nong and Kai formed the two wings; Murong Guo hid a thousand troops in a deep ravine and joined in great battle with Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Chui formed south of Hubi with Nong and Kai on the wings. Murong Guo hid a thousand men in a ravine and joined battle.

sentences.zh: 垂引軍偽退，永追奔數里，國發伏兵馳斷其後，楷、農夾擊之，永師大敗，斬首八千餘級，永奔還長子。

translations.literal: Chui led his army in a feigned retreat; Yong pursued several li; Guo's ambush galloped to cut his rear; Kai and Nong struck from both sides; Yong's army was greatly defeated, more than eight thousand heads were taken, and Yong fled back to Changzi.
translations.idiomatic: Chui feigned retreat. Yong pursued. Guo struck from behind; Kai and Nong closed on the flanks. Yong lost eight thousand men and fled to Changzi.

sentences.zh: 慕容贊攻克晉陽。

translations.literal: Murong Zan stormed and took Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Zan took Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 垂進圍長子，永將賈韜潛為內應。

translations.literal: Chui advanced to besiege Changzi; Yong's officer Jia Tao secretly acted as inner collaborator.
translations.idiomatic: Chui besieged Changzi. Yong's officer Jia Tao plotted treason within the walls.

sentences.zh: 垂進軍入城，永奔北門，為前驅所獲，於是數而戮之，並其所署公卿刁雲等三十餘人。

translations.literal: Chui advanced into the city; Yong fled to the north gate and was seized by the vanguard; thereupon he was enumerated and executed, together with more than thirty men including the dukes and ministers he had appointed, Diao Yun and others.
translations.idiomatic: Chui entered the city. Yong was seized at the north gate, condemned, and executed with more than thirty of his ministers including Diao Yun.

sentences.zh: 永所統新舊八郡戶七萬六千八百及乘輿、服御、伎樂、珍寶悉獲之，於是品物具矣。

translations.literal: The eight commanderies old and new under Yong's rule, seventy-six thousand eight hundred households, and the imperial carriage, regalia, musicians, and treasures were all captured; at this the categories of goods were complete.
translations.idiomatic: He took eight commanderies, seventy-six thousand eight hundred households, the imperial regalia, musicians, and treasure. The royal store was complete.

sentences.zh: 使慕容農略地河南，攻廩丘、陽城，皆克之，太山、琅邪諸郡皆委城奔潰，農進師臨海，置守宰而還。

translations.literal: He sent Murong Nong to reduce the lands of Henan, attacked Linqiu and Yangcheng, and took them all; the commanderies of Taishan and Langye all abandoned their cities and fled in rout; Nong advanced to the sea, set guards and magistrates, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Nong swept Henan, took Linqiu and Yangcheng, and drove the commanderies of Taishan and Langye to flight. He reached the sea, posted officials, and returned.

sentences.zh: 垂告捷于龍城之廟。

translations.literal: Chui reported victory at the temple in Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Chui reported victory at the Longcheng shrine.

sentences.zh: 遣其太子寶及農與慕容麟等率眾八萬伐魏，慕容德、慕容紹以步騎一萬八千為寶後繼。

translations.literal: He sent his crown prince Bao and Nong with Murong Lin and others leading eighty thousand troops to campaign against Wei; Murong De and Murong Shao with eighteen thousand foot and horse followed Bao as rear guard.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Bao and Nong with eighty thousand men against Wei. Murong De and Murong Shao followed with eighteen thousand as reserve.

sentences.zh: 魏聞寶將至，徙往河西。

translations.literal: When Wei heard Bao was coming, they moved west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Bao approached, the Wei moved west of the river.

sentences.zh: 寶進師臨河，懼不敢濟。

translations.literal: Bao advanced to the river bank and, fearing, did not dare cross.
translations.idiomatic: Bao reached the river but dared not cross.

sentences.zh: 還次參合，忽有大風黑氣，狀若堤防，或高或下，臨覆軍上。

translations.literal: Returning to camp at Canhe, suddenly a great wind and black vapor appeared, shaped like dikes and ramparts, now high now low, looming over the army.
translations.idiomatic: Marching back to Canhe, a black storm rose like a wall over the camp.

sentences.zh: 沙門支曇猛言於寶曰：「風氣暴迅，魏軍將至之候，宜遣兵禦之。

translations.literal: The monk Zhi Tanmeng said to Bao: "The wind is violent and swift—a sign the Wei army is coming; you ought to send troops to meet them."
translations.idiomatic: The monk Zhi Tanmeng warned Bao, "This wind means Wei is near. Send troops to meet them."

sentences.zh: 」寶笑而不納。

translations.literal: Bao laughed and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Bao laughed and ignored him.

sentences.zh: 曇猛固以為言，乃遣麟率騎三萬為後殿，以禦非常。

translations.literal: Tanmeng firmly pressed his view; thereupon he sent Lin with thirty thousand horse as rear guard to guard against the unforeseen.
translations.idiomatic: Tanmeng insisted. Bao sent Murong Lin with thirty thousand horse as rearguard.

sentences.zh: 麟以曇猛言為虛，縱騎遊獵。

translations.literal: Lin thought Tanmeng's words empty and let his horsemen roam in the hunt.
translations.idiomatic: Lin thought the warning nonsense and let his men hunt.

sentences.zh: 俄而黃霧四塞，日月晦冥，是夜魏師大至，三軍奔潰，寶與德等數千騎奔免，士眾還者十一二，紹死之。

translations.literal: Shortly yellow fog filled the four quarters, sun and moon were dim; that night the Wei army arrived in force; the three armies fled in rout; Bao and De and several thousand horsemen escaped; of the troops only one or two in ten returned; Shao died.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow fog blotted out the sky. That night Wei fell on them. The army broke. Bao and De escaped with a few thousand horse. Nine in ten perished. Shao was killed.

sentences.zh: 初，寶至幽州，所乘車軸無故自折。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Bao reached Youzhou, the axle of the carriage he rode broke for no reason.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao reached Youzhou, his carriage axle snapped without cause.

sentences.zh: 術士靳安以為大凶，固勸寶還，寶怒不從，故及於敗。

translations.literal: The diviner Jin An regarded it as great ill omen and firmly urged Bao to return; Bao grew angry and did not follow, and therefore met defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The diviner Jin An called it dire and begged Bao to turn back. Bao refused in anger—and met disaster.

sentences.zh: 寶恨參合之敗，屢言魏有可乘之機。

translations.literal: Bao hated the defeat at Canhe and repeatedly said Wei had an opportunity that could be seized.
translations.idiomatic: Smarting from Canhe, Bao kept saying Wei could be beaten.

sentences.zh: 慕容德亦曰：「魏人狃於參合之役，有陵太子之心，宜及聖略，摧其銳志。

translations.literal: Murong De also said: "The Wei men, accustomed to the battle at Canhe, harbor the will to look down on the crown prince; you ought, while the sacred strategy is at hand, to crush their sharp intent."
translations.idiomatic: Murong De said, "Wei thinks itself invincible after Canhe. Strike now and break their pride."

sentences.zh: 」垂從之，留德守中山，自率大眾出參合，鑿山開道，次於獵嶺。

translations.literal: Chui followed this, left De to guard Zhongshan, himself led the great host out of Canhe, cut through mountains to open a road, and halted at Lie Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Chui agreed. He left De at Zhongshan, led a great host from Canhe, cut a road through the mountains, and camped at Lie Ridge.

sentences.zh: 遣寶與農出天門，征北慕容隆、征西慕容盛逾青山，襲魏陳留公泥于平城，陷之，收其眾三萬餘人而還。

translations.literal: He sent Bao and Nong out from Tianmen, the pacifier of the north Murong Long and the general who campaigns west Murong Sheng crossed Green Mountain, and raided Wei's Duke of Chenliu Ni at Pingcheng, took it, and returned having gathered more than thirty thousand of his troops.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Bao and Nong through Tianmen, Long and Sheng over Green Mountain to storm Ni at Pingcheng, and returned with thirty thousand captives.

sentences.zh: 垂至參合，見往年戰處積骸如山，設弔祭之禮，死者父兄一時號哭，軍中皆慟。

translations.literal: When Chui reached Canhe he saw the old battlefield heaped with bones like a mountain; he established rites of mourning sacrifice; the fathers and elder brothers of the dead all wailed at once, and throughout the army there was grief.
translations.idiomatic: At Canhe the bones of the dead lay heaped like a hill. Chui mourned them. Fathers and brothers wailed, and the whole army wept.

sentences.zh: 垂慚憤歐血，因而寢疾，乘馬輿而進。

translations.literal: Chui in shame and rage vomited blood, and thereby fell ill; he advanced in a horse litter.
translations.idiomatic: Shame and rage made him vomit blood. He fell ill and rode in a litter.

sentences.zh: 過平城北三十里，疾篤，築燕昌城而還。

translations.literal: Passing thirty li north of Pingcheng his illness grew grave; he built Yanchang city and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty li north of Pingcheng his illness worsened. He built Yanchang city and turned back.

sentences.zh: 寶等至雲中，聞垂疾，皆引歸。

translations.literal: When Bao and the others reached Yunzhong and heard Chui was ill, they all turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Bao and the others, at Yunzhong, heard Chui was ill and turned back.

sentences.zh: 及垂至於平城，或有叛者奔告魏曰：「垂病已亡，輿屍在軍。

translations.literal: When Chui reached Pingcheng, some who rebelled fled to report to Wei: "Chui is dead from illness; his corpse is in the army on a litter."
translations.idiomatic: At Pingcheng deserters told Wei, "Chui is dead. His corpse travels in the litter."

sentences.zh: 」魏又聞參合大哭，以為信然，乃進兵追之，知平城已陷而退，還館陰山。

translations.literal: Wei also heard the great wailing at Canhe and believed it true; they advanced in pursuit; learning Pingcheng had fallen they withdrew and returned to lodge at Yin Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Wei heard the mourning at Canhe and believed Chui dead. They pursued until they learned Pingcheng had fallen, then withdrew to Yin Mountain.

sentences.zh: 垂至上谷之沮陽，乙太元二十一年死，時年七十一，凡在位十三年。

translations.literal: When Chui reached Juyang in Shanggu, in the twenty-first year of the Taiyuan era he died, aged seventy-one; altogether he held the throne thirteen years.
translations.idiomatic: At Juyang in Shanggu, in the twenty-first year of Taiyuan, Chui died at seventy-one, having ruled thirteen years.

sentences.zh: 遺令曰：「方今禍難尚殷，喪禮一從簡易，朝終夕殯，事訖成服，三日之後，釋服從政。

translations.literal: His final command said: "At present calamity and difficulty are still abundant; mourning rites should all follow simplicity—burial at evening of the day death comes at dawn, affairs concluded then don mourning garments; after three days, remove mourning and attend to government.
translations.idiomatic: His testament read: "Disaster still surrounds us. Keep mourning simple: bury at once, mourn three days, then return to rule.

sentences.zh: 強寇伺隙，秘勿發喪，至京然後舉哀行服。

translations.literal: Strong foes watch for openings—secretly do not announce the death; only when you reach the capital then raise the lament and don mourning garments."
translations.idiomatic: Enemies are near. Hide my death until you reach the capital, then mourn openly."

sentences.zh: 」寶等遵行之。

translations.literal: Bao and the others followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Bao and the others obeyed.

sentences.zh: 偽諡成武皇帝，廟號世祖，墓曰宣平陵。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Emperor Chengwu; his temple name Shizu; his tomb Xuanping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Emperor Chengwu, temple name Shizu, tomb Xuanping Mausoleum.
